title: Peter Berck's Contributions to Forestry Economics
venue: Sustainable Resource Development in the 21st Century
abstract: Peter Berck published numerous articles and book chapters related to the economics of forestry. His research covered, in approximate chronological order, four areas within forestry economics: (1) actual and optimal harvesting of timber, demand for timber, and, more generally, markets for wood products; (2) economic aspects of integrated management of forest pests; (3) old-growth redwoods, as a nonrenewable resource, and (4) impacts of timber harvesting and other aspects of forestry on income and employment in nearby communities. Interwoven in much of the research are analyses of effects of policy on efficiency and on forest-dependent communities.
abstract_zh: Peter Berck 发表了大量与林业经济学相关的文章和书籍章节。按大致的时间顺序，他的研究涵盖林业经济学的四个领域：（1）木材的实际和最优采伐、木材需求，以及更广泛的木制品市场；（2）森林害虫综合管理的经济学问题；（3）作为不可再生资源的古老红杉林；（4）木材采伐及其他林业活动对附近社区收入和就业的影响。在他的大部分研究中，都穿插着对政策对效率以及对依赖森林的社区影响的分析。

title: Farmer Interest in and Uses of Climate Forecasts for Florida and the Carolinas: Conditional Perspectives of Extension Personnel
abstract: In baseline surveys that were conducted in Florida, North Carolina, and South Carolina, extension personnel were asked whether, how, and which farmers would use climate forecasts to manage production and other aspects of their agribusinesses. In making such assessments extensionists use their expertise to account for, the authors assume, net benefits to farmers of the forecasts, given any help that they also expect to provide their clients. Models of conditional probabilities are estimated to show how the assessments depend on the expertise and other characteristics of the extensionist and her clientele. For example, if a person has worked at least 7 years in extension, she is more likely to agree or strongly agree that farmers are interested in using climate forecasts. An extensionist who works with field crop producers is more likely than one who does not to think that a farmer can use climate forecasts to improve planting schedules, harvest planning, crop selection, nutrient management, and land allocation. An extensionist is more likely to assess that farmers who produce particular crops can use climate forecasts to be more successful if she works with them. An extensionist whose clientele’s average farm size exceeds 200 acres is more likely to indicate that a farmer can use climate forecasts to improve irrigation management, harvest planning, and crop selection. In addition to serving as references for future work, these conditional assessments almost always provide more nuanced and useful information than unconditional ones about potential farmer interest in and uses of climate forecasts for the three-state region.
abstract_zh: 在佛罗里达州、北卡罗来纳州和南卡罗来纳州开展的基线调查中，推广人员被问及农民是否会、如何以及哪些农民会使用气候预报来管理生产和农业经营的其他方面。在做出此类评估时，推广人员运用其专业知识，并假定（作者如此假设）预报能为农民带来净收益，同时考虑了他们自己预计向客户提供的帮助。我们估计了条件概率模型，以展示这些评估如何取决于推广人员的专业知识及其他特征，以及其客户群体的特征。例如，若某人在推广服务工作了至少 7 年，她更可能同意或强烈同意农民对使用气候预报感兴趣。与不服务于大田作物生产者的推广人员相比，服务于大田作物生产者的推广人员更可能认为，农民可以利用气候预报改进播种时间、收获计划、作物选择、养分管理和土地配置。推广人员更可能评估认为，若其服务的对象是特定作物的生产者，这些生产者可以利用气候预报获得更大的成功。若推广人员所服务的客户平均农场规模超过 200 英亩，她更可能指出，农民可以利用气候预报改进灌溉管理、收获计划和作物选择。除了为未来的研究提供参考，这些条件评估几乎总能比无条件的评估提供更为细致和有用的信息，帮助了解农民对气候预报在该三州地区的潜在兴趣和用途。

Estimating Economic Activity and Impacts of Urban Forestry in California with Multiple Data Sources from the Early 1990s
abstract: Urban forests provide tree products and aesthetic, recreational, health, and environmental benefits. Yet the expenditures that people make to secure these benefits are difficult to estimate for lack of comprehensive published data. Based on various sources of data, we estimate that Californians spent at least $947 million to obtain these benefits and the state’s urban forestry “sector” had sales of at least $1,115 billion in a 12-month period in the early 1990s. As a result of direct, indirect, and induced effects, urban forestry accounted for at least $3,384 billion in total sales. This level of sales became about $1,869 billion in annual income to individuals and supported about 57,200 jobs in this period within the state. Knowledge of this economic activity is important, in principle, to voters and public decision-makers who allocate human resources, tax revenue, and water for the management of community forests and other natural resources in California.
abstract_zh: 城市森林提供树木产品，以及审美、娱乐、健康和环境效益。然而，由于缺乏全面的公开数据，人们为获取这些效益所支出的费用很难估算。基于多种数据来源，我们估计，在 20 世纪 90 年代初的 12 个月期间，加利福尼亚人至少支出了 9.47 亿美元以获取这些效益，而该州的城市林业“部门”的销售额至少为 11,150 亿美元。由于直接、间接和引致效应，城市林业产生的总销售额至少为 33,840 亿美元。这一销售水平在该时期转化为个人年收入约 18,690 亿美元，并在该州支撑了约 57,200 个就业岗位。了解这一经济活动，原则上对选民和公共决策者非常重要，他们需要为社区森林和其他自然资源的管理分配人力资源、税收收入和水资源。

title: Urban Forestry Adds $3.8 Billion in Sales to California Economy
abstract: Urban forests provide tree products and aesthetic, recreational, health and environmental benefits. Californians spent at least $1.080 billion to obtain these benefits and the state's urban forestry sector had sales of at least $1.248 billion in a 12-month period in the early 1990s. As a result of ripple effects, urban forestry accounted for at least $3.789 billion in total sales, $2.092 billion in income to individuals, and 64,000 jobs in this period in the state. Knowledge of this economic activity is necessary for voters and government officials who make decisions that affect management of these and other natural resources in California.
abstract_zh: 城市森林提供树木产品，以及审美、娱乐、健康和环境效益。在 20 世纪 90 年代初的 12 个月期间，加利福尼亚人至少花费了 10.80 亿美元以获取这些效益，而该州城市林业部门的销售额至少为 12.48 亿美元。由于连带效应（ripple effects），城市林业产生的总销售额至少为 37.89 亿美元，个人收入为 20.92 亿美元，并在该州创造了 64,000 个就业岗位。了解这一经济活动，对于做出影响这些及其他自然资源管理的决策的选民和政府官员而言是必要的。
